name: Utah
summary: Statutes: le.utah.gov (Utah Legislature). Each section URL serves a JavaScript shell; the text sits in a versioned file (C{title}-{chapter}-S{section}_{effective}.html) whose name you reach by following index hops. fetch_doc.py reads those files, and also the per-title PDFs (Title 78B: 456 pp). Justia 2025 is a constructible tier-2 fallback that WebFetch reads. Constitution: le.utah.gov uses the same versioned-file scheme. Court rules: legacy.utcourts.gov/rules/view.php gives one constructible HTML page per rule for every rule set. Admin Code: adminrules.utah.gov is a JavaScript app with no text for the script; Cornell LII has constructible per-section pages, and the Utah State Bulletin PDFs on rules.utah.gov are readable. Case law: utcourts.gov opinion PDFs are disallowed by robots.txt, so read opinions on Justia (public-domain cites with ¶ numbers). Certiorari dispositions are in bimonthly PDFs on www.utcourts.gov, listed by Court of Appeals docket number.

citation_map.notes: Utah adopted public-domain citations in 1999 (YYYY UT N for the Supreme Court, YYYY UT App N for the Court of Appeals). Pinpoints are paragraph cites (¶ N), and the P.2d/P.3d parallel cite follows. Court of Appeals memorandum decisions take UT App numbers too. Pre-2011 'unpublished decisions' are usually cited with a trailing U (e.g. 2008 UT App 400U); that form is from memory and unverified. Bare 'UT' is distinctive to Utah. Statute section numbers have three parts, TITLE-CHAPTER-SECTION, and title and chapter can carry a letter (78B-2-307, 41-6a-502, 26B-3-102). Other states (e.g. Colorado C.R.S. 13-80-102) use similar three-part numbers, so the statute regex requires 'Utah Code' or 'U.C.A.' first. A range like '§§ 78B-2-301 to -307' matches only the first section. 'Utah Code Jud. Admin.' and 'UCJA' are court rules, not statutes: the statute regex does not match them, because a section number must follow 'Utah Code' directly. Bare 'Rule 12' or 'Rule 702' must not route here without 'Utah' context. Rules of Professional Conduct are numbered N.N in citations, but the URL key is scrp rule 3-N.0N (Rule 1.7 → 3-1.07; Rule 1.10 → 3-1.10 unverified). Admin Code citations begin with an R number (R414-1-1). A bare 'R414-1-1' is not routed without 'Utah Admin. Code'. Docket numbers are 8 digits (filing year + sequence), sometimes with a -CA or -SC suffix; they are generic and context_required. CourtListener ids (utah, utahctapp) are from memory. Georgia's 'Code Section NN-N-NNN' pattern also matches the prose form 'Utah Code section 76-5-203' (case-insensitive), so an explicit 'Utah' marker must win in routing. Juvenile (urjp), Small Claims (srpe) and Business & Chancery (urbcp) rules route with an explicit 'Utah' marker; the bare short forms URJP/URBCP are context_required.

sources.title: Utah Code (le.utah.gov)
sources.publisher: Utah State Legislature, Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel
sources.official_status_evidence: https://le.utah.gov/documents/disclaimer.htm: the Legislature 'attempt[s] to ensure' the online information is accurate and gives access on a strictly 'as is' basis. No UELMA authentication statement was found.
sources.coverage: Whole Utah Code (Titles 3–81) with the current version of each section and an effective date. The per-section version files offer PDF, RTF and XML downloads, and the per-title PDFs hold whole titles.

access.pattern_rules: The shell URL is constructible. Title is written as cited (78B, 26B), chapter folder upper-case (Chapter6A), file name keeps the citation's case (41-6a-S102): e.g. 78B-2-307 → /xcode/Title78B/Chapter2/78B-2-S307.html; 41-6a-102 → /xcode/Title41/Chapter6A/41-6a-S102.html. The shell has NO text: its JavaScript sets versionDefault="C78B-2-S307_2023050320230503", and the text lives in that file name + .html in the same folder. {version} is two 8-digit dates (YYYYMMDD twice; 1800010118000101 = unamended since recodification). It cannot be derived from the citation. fetch_doc.py strips scripts, so it cannot read versionDefault. Get the version id from the Part (or Chapter) index file's section link instead: '78B-2-S307.html?v=C78B-2-S307_2023050320230503'. Part number = the section's hundreds digit (307 → P3) in most chapters.
access.navigation: Code index file C_1800010118000101.html → Title link '?v=C78B_1800010118000101' → fetch /xcode/Title78B/C78B_1800010118000101.html → Chapter link '?v=C78B-2_…' → fetch /xcode/Title78B/Chapter2/C78B-2_1800010118000101.html (lists Parts, no section ranges) → Part link '?v=C78B-2-P3_…' → fetch C78B-2-P3_1800010118000101.html (lists every section with its ?v= id) → fetch C78B-2-S307_2023050320230503.html (body). Rule: take the ?v= value, append .html, and fetch it in the same folder. Chapters without parts list their sections directly. Version ids below the title level vary (e.g. C63G-20_2015051220150512, C63G-2-S201_2026050620260701): ALWAYS copy the ?v= value from the parent index; never assume _1800010118000101. Hop tool: `fetch_doc.py links <index-url> <filter>` (e.g. filter 'S307').

automation.notes: WebFetch on the shell URL returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (permission not answered). The shell would give WebFetch no text anyway. Version files are small (about 2–5K chars) and fetch_doc.py reads them in full. XML per section (C…_{version}.xml) gives clean text with history ('Amended by Chapter 185, 2023 General Session'). The whole-title PDF (C78B_1800010118000101.pdf) is 456 pp and 1.5M chars.
